jurisdictions.name: Kent County (Dover area, unincorporated)
jurisdictions.office: Kent County Department of Planning Services, Building Permits
notes: A permit is required for above-ground and in-ground pools, hot tubs and spas.
The county publishes a pool permit guide and a Pool Barrier Requirements Brochure on its building permit information page.
Kent County lists the 2018 International Residential Code with county amendments as adopted, and its page names no swimming pool code edition.
Fences over 7 feet need a permit except when enclosing a swimming pool area; zoning rules still apply.

jurisdictions.name: Milford
jurisdictions.office: City of Milford Building Inspections & Permitting
notes: The division handles building permits and inspections for residential work, and its page lists fee schedules and guidelines for pools among other project types.
Building permits, inspection scheduling and licenses are handled through the city's Civic Access portal.
The page references the 2018 International Building Code, International Residential Code and International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.

jurisdictions.name: Newark
jurisdictions.office: City of Newark Code Enforcement Division
notes: The city's Forms and Applications page directs building permit applicants to its online self-service portal.
The page lists a downloadable Building Permit Application under the Code Enforcement Division; it has no pool-specific permit page.

jurisdictions.name: New Castle County (unincorporated)
jurisdictions.office: New Castle County Department of Land Use
notes: The county says a permit is required for all pools, spas and hot tubs that are 24 inches and above in height or are designed and manufactured to be connected to a circulation system, when they are intended for swimming, bathing or wading.

The county's pool permit requirements sheet says in-ground pool drawings must meet ISPSC standards, particularly for minimum depths to support diving boards, ladders and stairs. In-ground pools also need a Lines and Grades plan and the latest Residential L&G Checklist, both signed and sealed by a Delaware licensed engineer or surveyor. The plan is to include any pool heater, overhead wires with any relocation shown, a plan for excess material disposal, the pool fence, construction equipment access and all drainage and sewer easements.

The same sheet says a private swimming pool may be in the rear yard if the pool and all appurtenances, such as decking, the pool filter and pump, are at least 6 feet from any side or rear property line. All pools must be at least 10 feet horizontally from overhead wires, and no pool or hot tub is permitted in any easement or building setback lines.

The county's code page lists the 2024 International Residential Code and the 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code as effective January 1, 2026. It says Chapter 6 of the County Code and its appendices contain amendments to the adopted codes.
